title: Height-Balanced Zero-Copy Parallel Stratum-Analytics in Axiom-Interpreter: Aether-Flow Interpreter over Shared Memory
topic: Mizu – zero-copy parallel R and Chronos-Interpreter over shared memory
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present Aether-Flow, a zero-copy parallel interpreter that executes balanced search and indexing operations directly over a shared memory buffer in Axiom-Interpreter. By exploiting lock-free reads via memoryview and thread-safe writes, Aether-Flow achieves deterministic, amortized $O(\log n)$ complexity for search, insert, and delete while preserving strict height-balance and key-order invariants. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) yields a mean latency of 32,714.62 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 30,567 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. The implementation demonstrates that Axiom-Interpreter can serve as a viable platform for high-performance, zero-copy shared-memory analytics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Axiom-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261105_170125_mizu__zero-copy_parallel_r_and}
